survey: A single cowboy hat in three-quarter view, seen from moderately above. The wide brim is a flat, gently curled disc whose top face is fully visible. The left and front edge curls up slightly, and the right side sweeps back to an upturned point. A cream piping rim runs around the brim's whole edge with a steady thickness. The crown rises vertically from the brim's centre-back and has a pinched dent on top. A red band wraps the base of the crown, and its lower edge curves downward across the front, which is right for a cylinder seen from above. The band's curve is about as deep as the brim's open oval, so crown and brim share one viewing angle. The crown's sides stay close to vertical. The brim's back edge disappears behind the crown and comes back out on the right, which makes sense. The hat floats on a radial background with no ground plane, so there is no contact surface to check.
